title: Riley Green’s ‘That’s Just Me’: All 19 Tracks Ranked
summary: The recent Billboard cover star aims to continue his winning streak on new album.
contentText:
Riley Green has steadily forged a reputation as a multimedia artist and businessperson, taking on a role as a coach on The Voice and previously landing a role on the Yellowstone spinoff Marshals . He launched Duck Club Bourbon last year and in 2024 opened Riley Green’s Duck Blind in Nashville. Those roles build on the headliner status he’s already built over the past several years. He was also just revealed as a headliner at 2027’s California’s country music festival Stagecoach, alongside Zach Top and Garth Brooks.

And yet, he’s remained focused on the main thing: continuing to cement his reputation as a musical purveyor of timeless-feeling country songs, and a writer on many of them, in the tradition of artists such as Alan Jackson and Toby Keith.

Related

After Slow-Burn Rise, Riley Green Is Red Hot: ‘If This Had Happened To Me When I Was 22, It Would Have Been Mayhem’

Green’s fourth studio album That’s Just Me , which arrived Friday (Sept. 18) via Nashville Harbor Records & Entertainment, focuses heavily on heartbreak, longing, temptation and also romantic freedom, while elsewhere leaning into stories of small-town nostalgia and nodding to the wanderlust of musicians and creatives.

The album follows Green’s Don’t Mind If I Do , which included the Billboard Country Airplay chart-toppers “Worst Way” and the album’s title track. Don’t Mind If I Do reached the top 10 on Billboard’s Top Country Albums chart last year, and to date, he’s earned four Country Airplay chart-topping hits.

The recent Billboard cover star ’s new album, produced by Dann Huff, aims to continue his winning streak, balancing the heartbreak songs with comedic gems. He is a writer on the bulk of the songs, including five solo writes. The album is also solidly collaborative, with Green welcoming Hannah McFarland, Jake Worthington, Brooks & Dunn and Alabama’s Randy Owen. In the album’s initial radio single release, “Think as You Drunk” (which is at No. 13 on the Country Airplay chart), Green pays homage to another musical influence: the late Keith.

Below, Billboard ranks all 19 tracks on Green’s new album That’s Just Me , from good to best.
